corrections.from:
Ps 140, 2–4
Let my prayer, O Lord, like incense before You; the lifting up of my hands, like the evening sacrifice.
O Lord, set a watch before my mouth, a guard at the door of my lips.
Let not my heart incline to the evil of engaging in deeds of wickedness.
corrections.to:
Ps 140, 2–4
Let my prayer rise before Thee as incense, O Lord; let the lifting up of my hands be as the evening sacrifice.
O Lord, set a watch before my mouth, a guard at the door of my lips.
Let not my heart incline to words of malice, to make excuses for sins.
corrections.reference: Coalition in Support of Ecclesia Dei, Latin-English Booklet Missal (2013), printed p. 25, PDF p. 26 (poetic translation); Latin Dirigatur oratio mea verified against same booklet PDF p. 25; expanded comparison: Psalm 140:2–4, Latin verba malitiae and ad excusandas excusationes in peccatis; Red Missal scanned p.26/printed p.25.
corrections.decision: Both opening missing-verb grammar and final verse wrong semantic omission repaired under one exact source-owned C0122 English correction. Preserve immutable donor, full Psalm source path and section identity.

corrections.from:
There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to give testimony of the light,
that all men might believe through him. He was not the light, but was to give testimony of the light. That was the true light,
which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not.
He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. But as many as received Him, He gave them power to be made the sons of God,
to them that believe in His name: who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
corrections.to:
There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to give testimony of the light,
that all men might believe through him. He was not the light, but was to give testimony of the light. That was the true light,
which enlighteneth every man that cometh into this world. He was in the world, and the world was made by Him, and the world knew Him not.
He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. But as many as received Him, to them He gave power to become the sons of God;
to them that believe in His name: who are born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
corrections.reference: Coalition in Support of Ecclesia Dei, Latin–English Booklet Missal 2013, Last Gospel, PDF page 50, printed page 49; compare original John 1:12–14 Latin on PDF page 49.
corrections.decision: Adopt more faithful Red relative-clause form of Latin dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri, without changing speaker identity.
